name: ct_head_cerebellar_haemorrhage
clinical_history:
onset at 13:30 with left facial droop, left arm and leg weakness and slurred speech.
BP 255/161
findings:
- There is a large area of parenchymal hemorrhage in the right cerebellum measuring 5 cm in diameter with significant peri-lesional vasogenic edema and this is causing major midline shift across the horizontal cerebellar axis with complete effacement of the cerebral aqueduct and fourth ventricle and crowding of the foramen magnum due to ipsilateral tonsillar herniation

- There is some regional subarachnoid and subdural extension of haemorrhage along the tentorium

- The background brain parenchyma otherwise appears unremarkable with no gross areas of infarction

- Background chronic small vessel ischemic changes and age-appropriate involutional atrophy are noted with asymmetric predominance of the right frontal lobe

name: ct_tap_acute_abdomen_gda_bleed
clinical_history: 72F, admitted 4 days ago with confusion and falls. Background AF on apixaban, T2DM, previous right MCA stroke with residual left hemiparesis. Today developed acute abdominal pain localised to epigastrium with associated vomiting. Lactate 4.2, Hb dropped from 112 to 87 over 24 hours. Query mesenteric ischaemia, query GI bleed source, query intra-abdominal pathology. Previous imaging includes CT head on admission (old infarct only) and an abdominal ultrasound 6 months ago (fatty liver, small abdominal aortic aneurysm 3.8cm infrarenal).
findings:
Scan performed thorax abdomen pelvis portal venous phase, no arterial phase obtained
Large volume haemoperitoneum throughout abdomen and pelvis, highest density in pelvis and around liver
Active contrast extravasation from gastroduodenal artery branch, approximately 2cm distal to origin, forming a small pseudoaneurysm approximately 8mm
Duodenum D1/D2 shows wall thickening and mural gas, adjacent fat stranding
Infrarenal abdominal aortic aneurysm now measures 4.6cm, previously 3.8cm on US 6 months ago, no evidence of rupture or contained leak
Pancreas appears atrophic with pancreatic duct dilation to 6mm, calcifications within pancreatic head, consistent with chronic pancreatitis
Multiple small hypodensities in both kidneys, largest 1.2cm right interpolar, not fully characterised on this phase
Large hiatus hernia with approximately 40% of stomach intrathoracic
Bilateral dependent atelectasis, small right pleural effusion
Left adrenal thickening, nodular, 2.4cm, not previously characterised
Cholelithiasis, no wall thickening
Moderate bilateral pelvic free fluid continuous with the haemoperitoneum
Old right MCA territory encephalomalacia visible on scout images only
Bladder partially distended, catheter not yet placed
Diffuse colonic faecal loading
Background mild-moderate atherosclerosis

items.text: Triage: Mesenteric ischaemia (arterial embolic, venous thrombotic, non-occlusive, or acute-on-chronic atherosclerotic); GI haemorrhage source (upper GI, lower GI, mesenteric, or retroperitoneal); intra-abdominal catastrophe (AAA rupture, perforation, obstruction, abscess)

items.text: Non-occlusive mesenteric ischaemia — diffuse SMA or celiac narrowing without focal occlusion, bowel wall enhancement loss in watershed distribution (splenic flexure, rectosigmoid)

name: ctpa_acute_pe_rv_strain
clinical_history: 58M, sudden onset pleuritic chest pain and dyspnoea, SpO2 91% on air, HR 112, D-dimer 4.2, Wells score 6. Query PE.
findings:
- Filling defects right main pulmonary artery extending into lower lobe segmental branches
- Further filling defect left lower lobe segmental artery
- RV:LV ratio 1.2, interventricular septal flattening
- Small right pleural effusion
- Mosaic attenuation right lower lobe, no consolidation
- No pericardial effusion
- Incidental 5mm right upper lobe pulmonary nodule
- Thyroid and imaged upper abdomen unremarkable

name: ct_ap_diverticulitis_abscess
clinical_history: 66F, 4 days left iliac fossa pain, fever 38.2, WCC 15, CRP 180. Query diverticulitis.
findings:
- Sigmoid diverticulosis with segmental wall thickening over 6cm
- Pericolic fat stranding
- 3.2cm rim-enhancing pericolic collection adjacent to sigmoid
- No free intraperitoneal gas
- Trace pelvic free fluid only
- Ureters not obstructed
- Liver, spleen, pancreas, adrenals, kidneys unremarkable
- No suspicious osseous lesion

items.text: Triage: Acute diverticulitis (confirm or exclude) versus alternative aetiologies of left iliac fossa pain (colorectal malignancy, epiploic appendagitis, ovarian pathology, ureteric calculus, ischaemic colitis, abscess of other origin)
items.label: P

items.text: Uncomplicated (Hinchey I) — pericolic fat stranding, diverticula at inflamed segment, no collection, no extraluminal air
items.label: X

items.text: Pericolic/paracolic abscess (Hinchey II) — walled-off rim-enhancing fluid collection adjacent to inflamed segment, ± internal air-fluid level
items.label: P

items.text: Generalised peritonitis (Hinchey III) — free peritoneal fluid of mixed attenuation, extraluminal air beyond pericolic region, diffuse mesenteric and peritoneal stranding
items.label: X

items.text: Distant abscess (Hinchey II variant) — rim-enhancing collection in pelvis, subhepatic space, or other non-adjacent location
items.label: O

items.text: Stricture / partial obstruction — luminal narrowing at inflamed segment with proximal colonic dilatation
items.label: O

items.text: Fistula — abnormal enhancing tract from inflamed segment to bladder, vagina, adjacent bowel loop, or abdominal wall
items.label: O

items.text: Colorectal malignancy — eccentric or concentric wall thickening >1 cm, luminal narrowing, heterogeneous enhancement, mesorectal or mesenteric lymphadenopathy
items.label: O

items.text: Epiploic appendagitis — oval fat-density lesion with hyperdense rim adjacent to colonic serosa
items.label: X

items.text: Ovarian pathology (postmenopausal) — adnexal mass, complex free fluid
items.label: X

items.text: Ureteric calculus — hyperdense focus in ureter with proximal hydroureter
items.label: X

items.text: Ischaemic colitis — segmental wall thickening in a watershed distribution, thumbprinting, mesenteric vessel involvement
items.label: X

items.text: Sigmoid diverticulitis (uncomplicated): "The sigmoid colon shows focal circumferential wall thickening to 8 mm over a 4 cm segment at the sigmoid–descending junction, with surrounding pericolic fat stranding extending 3 cm. Several diverticula are visible at the affected segment. No pericolic abscess, extraluminal air, or fistula is identified."
items.label: K

items.text: Pericolic abscess: "A 3.2 cm rim-enhancing fluid collection is seen posterior to the inflamed sigmoid segment, with a small internal air-fluid level, consistent with a pericolic abscess."
items.label: K

items.text: Colorectal mass (alternative diagnosis): "The rectosigmoid junction shows a 3.4 cm eccentric, irregular wall thickening with luminal narrowing to 8 mm and heterogeneous enhancement, with three enlarged mesorectal lymph nodes (largest 14 mm short axis)."
items.label: R

items.text: Free perforation: "Extraluminal air tracks along the left paracolic gutter with moderate-volume free peritoneal fluid of mixed attenuation, consistent with free perforation."
items.label: R
